method: Each batch is seven interleaved 30-emulated-second c3-hello runs after one excluded warmup per arm, reversing arm order in even rounds. CPU is getrusage user + system. Separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR per arm; fixed frozen binaries. The final comparisons use main plus one candidate, or C3 plus UART.
aggregation: All completed two-arm batches of the selected binaries are pooled within each comparison. C3/main includes the original pilot and two confirmation batches; both UART comparisons contain two fixed batches. No individual sample or completed matching batch was discarded. The earlier five-arm comparison is retained separately and excluded from the two-arm aggregation.
limits: Pooled medians meet the requested +0.5% bound and ranges overlap; individual batch medians do not all meet it. This is a local CPU-time result with visible between-batch variation, not a universal zero-cost guarantee.

Every accepted run starts below one-minute load 3; captured post-run values are also below 3. The original pilot checked load before each run but did not retain the exact pre-run reading; its maximum captured post-run load was 1.1871. Later batches retain both readings.
Each run has 4.8 billion instructions/cycles, zero exceptions, 3028 interrupts and identical console SHA-256. No browser or hardware timing claim.
Raw process identities, local paths and loaded-image lists are omitted. Numeric samples and original artifact hashes remain unchanged.

receipt.measurement: resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) user + system CPU seconds around one completed CLI subprocess; seven samples per arm after one excluded warmup; reverse order in even rounds
limitations: Local macOS arm64 CPU-time comparison, not browser or hardware timing.
No process inventory retained; uptime one-minute load is below 3 before every subprocess, and rounded post-run load is also below 3. Aggregate load cannot exclude all brief contention.
All arms use unchanged native scheduling and identical firmware, instructions, cycles and console hash.
